review_scope: Read-only source/protocol/contract and prepared-artifact audit before timing. No benchmark runs or builds by this review. Final adoption and exact-final-header validation remain separate.
source_findings: All four variants accept measured long-long coordinate inputs through the public bound and produce normalized distinct original indices or the small-input sentinel. Equal objectives, not equal tie choices, are compared.
Independent singleton checks run before returns and all actual rejection statuses were SIGABRT. Fast-cases also validates N=2 and all-identical shortcuts in debug mode.

Index and 24-byte-record hulls deduplicate by coordinates, preserve an original representative and remove non-left turns. Calipers use widened exact edge cross products and squared distances with parallel-support endpoints retained.

Full baseline and wrapper calls use the exact snapshotted public header. Separately timed int-index calipers are explicitly an independent explanatory decomposition, not additive production-stage timings.

All input generation, result objective validation and hull metadata lie outside kernel timers. Full calls include local storage destruction; separate stage timers do not claim to sum to full elapsed time.

Main measurement writes raw warmup and measured rows before identity rejection, preserves subprocess/schema failures, and refuses replacement of existing experiment or measurement directories. Missing stages remain null; summaries do not replace missing values with zero.

I/O comparison separates parse, solve and format with the same input files. End-to-end includes process/pipe/validation overhead. Allocation runs are separate; requested bytes and whole-process RSS are accurately scoped.
limits: Concrete benchmark inputs use long long only; smaller signed template types are covered by separate library validation, not these candidate timings.
Small all-pairs benchmark oracle shares its widened squared-distance helper with candidate comparison; the library also has a separate int256 permanent oracle and independent proof review.
Current negative checks actually returned SIGABRT, but the runner accepts any nonzero termination; timeout or another crash would need manual rejection.

Current 240 small rows passed and are retained. A hypothetical early small-profile JSON/schema failure saves its rejected subprocess but not earlier accumulated small rows. This limitation does not affect preserved measurement JSONL rows.
Shared unpinned host and five measured repetitions per cell; no fastest-submission ranking or universal improvement is claimed.
Final numerical review must retain unchanged-stage regressions, missing values and all original samples; no timing outcome is established by this pre-review.
